```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(arrow); library(tidyverse); library(lubridate) ; library(dplyr) ; library(easystats)
# set the default plot style
theme_set(theme_minimal())
install.packages(c("gt", "webshot2"))
library(gt)
```

```{r}
#load in data
smarvus_complete <- read_csv("cleaned_smarvus.csv")
smarvus_complete
```
```{r}
#Removing pupils who didn't answer STARS (Q7.1) R-MARS-S (7.2) STARS-M (8.1) or R-MARS (8.2)
#Identify all anxiety questionnaire columns

anxiety_cols <- c(
  paste0("Q7.1_", 1:23),
  paste0("Q7.2_", 1:19),
  paste0("Q8.1_", 1:20),
  paste0("Q8.2_", 1:20)
)

#Remove students with any missing anxiety responses
smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_complete |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(anxiety_cols), ~ !is.na(.)))

print(nrow(smarvus_complete) - nrow(smarvus_filtered))

#grouping northern ireland and england to the uk
smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_filtered |>
  mutate(country = if_else(
    country %in% c("England", "Northern Ireland"),
    "United Kingdom",
    country
  ))

#finding number of responses, languages and unis
country_table <- smarvus_filtered |>
  count(country, language, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    country = "Country",
    language = "Survey Language",
    n = "Students",
    proportion = "Percentage"
  ) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = proportion, decimals = 1)

country_table

gtsave(country_table, "country_table.png")
```
The SMARVUS dataset was initially cleaned by removing variables that were either not relevant to the research question or contained very little information. Only students whose grades were provided directly by their universities were included to minimise potential self-reporting bias and ensure consistency in comparisons, as self-reported grades could relate to different stages of a student's degree. Observations where the university-reported grade was zero were also excluded. Demographic and educational information, such as gender, language and previous level of mathematics study, was retained.

The dataset was then further filtered by excluding the 70 respondents who did not fully complete all four anxiety questionnaires (STARS, R-MARS-S, STARS-M and R-MARS). This left a final sample of 1,728 students across 20 universities in 11 countries, with questionnaires completed in eight languages.
